pages.title: Floating actions and window
pages.html:
Floating actions and window

FloatingDock places a page’s floating actions at the bottom end and the one window an action opens above them. FloatingActions is the capsule; FloatingAction an action with its count and attention dot, pressed while its window is open. FloatingWindow sizes to its content up to the space above the actions.

1 / 2

“Corners are small: 2px on controls, 4px on surfaces.”

sample-lead Agree on 2/4. Counts keep the same radius.

Usage

import { FloatingDock, FloatingActions, FloatingAction, FloatingWindow, FloatingWindowAction } from '@tmt/browser-ui/ui';

<FloatingDock top={headerHeight}>
  {open && (
    <FloatingWindow key={open} open label="Discussion" onClose={close} header={<>…<FloatingWindowAction label="Resolve" icon={<Check />} /></>}>
      …
    </FloatingWindow>
  )}
  <FloatingActions label="Page actions">
    <FloatingAction label="Comments (2)" icon={<MessagesSquare />} count={2} expanded={open === 'comments'} onClick={toggle} />
  </FloatingActions>
</FloatingDock>

Variants and states

Closed

Keyboard contract

  • Opening moves focus into the window; Esc or Close closes it through one onClose.
  • Focus returns to the action that opened it. Key the window by that action.
  • An open menu, select or tooltip inside takes the first Esc; only the next one closes the window.
  • A composing (IME), repeated or modified Esc never closes it.
  • One window at a time; its action reads as pressed (aria-expanded) while open.

pages.title: Rich input
pages.html:
Rich input

One Lexical editor in two shapes: the single-line search with filter chips and the multi-line composer with mentions, a toolbar and an attachment slot. It ships in its own entry, so pages without it never load Lexical.

Usage

import { RichInput, emptyRichInputValue } from '@tmt/browser-ui/rich-input';

<RichInput shape="multi" label="Message" value={value} onChange={setValue} onSubmit={send}
  suggestions={[{ kind: 'mention', trigger: '@', options: (query) => … }]} />

Variants and states

Composer

Optional search props

PropBehavior
onSuggestionChooseReturn true to handle a suggestion as an action instead of inserting a chip; receives the edited value without the query.
onChipRemoveReceives the resulting value when a chip is removed.
onEscapeHandles Escape when no suggestion list is open.

Keyboard contract

  • Enter submits; Shift+Enter adds a line in the composer.
  • A trigger opens suggestions: arrows move, Enter or Tab inserts the chip.
  • Esc closes the suggestion list and stops there, so a window around stays open.
  • Backspace after a chip removes it; nothing acts during an IME composition. Optional onChipRemove reports the edited value to its host.
  • Optional onSuggestionChoose can handle a suggestion as an action instead of inserting a chip; onEscape handles Escape when no list is open.
  • Paste is plain text; on the single line a pasted break becomes a space.

pages.title: Block shell
pages.html:
Block shell

Every block sits in the shell, and the shell draws nothing at rest: no border, fill or box, so the page reads as one document. Hover gives a light tint and selection a deeper one, never a border; the focus ring shows only for the keyboard. Each editor renders one BlockHandle (insert and the block menu, which is also the drag grip) inside the hovered or focused block, in the gutter 8px to its left. Under 480px of document width the handle hides: a tap selects and a long press opens the block menu as a sheet.

Idle: no handle, no fill.

Hover: the tint, and the one shared handle in the gutter.

Selected: the selection tint, no border.

Usage

import { BlockDocument, Block, BlockHandle, BlockDropLine, BlockGhost, blockKeyAction } from '@tmt/browser-ui/blocks';

<BlockDocument>
  <Block label="Table: Ticket status" kind="table" selected={selected} tabIndex={-1}
    onKeyDown={(event) => run(blockKeyAction(event, selecting))}>
    {hovered && <BlockHandle onInsert={openInsert} onMenu={openMenu} onGripPointerDown={startDrag} />}
    <TableBlock … />
  </Block>
</BlockDocument>
// While dragging: the dragged block takes state="dragging", BlockDropLine marks the landing place
// and BlockGhost follows the pointer.

Variants and states

1440, light and dark

390, light and dark

Keyboard contract (blockKeyAction)

  • Menu, Shift+F10 or Cmd/Ctrl+/ open the block menu from the focused block; the handle is not in the Tab order.
  • Esc leaves typing and selects the block; ↑ and ↓ move the selection, Shift+↑↓ extend it.
  • Alt+Shift+↑↓ move the selection; Cmd/Ctrl+D duplicates; Delete deletes; Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes.

Do and don't

Do

Render one handle per editor and move it to the hovered or focused block.

Don’t

Draw a border or a resting fill around a block; only the card block has a frame.
pages.description: Every block sits in the shell, and the shell draws nothing at rest: no border, fill or box, so the page reads as one document. Hover gives a light tint and selection a deeper one, never a border; the focus ring shows only for the keyboard. Each editor renders one BlockHandle (insert and the block menu, which is also the drag grip) inside the hovered or focused block, in the gutter 8px to its left. Under 480px of document width the handle hides: a tap selects and a long press opens the block menu as a sheet.
dos: Render one handle per editor and move it to the hovered or focused block.
Draw a border or a resting fill around a block; only the card block has a frame.

pages.title: Block menus
pages.html:
Block menus

BlockMenu is the insert menu (a listbox opened by / or the handle’s +, filtered as the person types) and, with kind="actions", the block menu (Move to…, Move up, Move down, Duplicate, Copy link to block, @ this block in a comment, Delete; never "turn into"). Focus stays in the editor: the host drives the active item with nextBlockMenuItem and names it with activeId. On a phone it is a bottom sheet with 44px rows.

See the frames below: a floating menu needs its own page.

Usage

import { BlockMenu, BlockMenuGroup, BlockMenuItem, BlockMenuSeparator, BlockMenuEmpty, BlockMenuFooter, BlockKbd, blockActions, nextBlockMenuItem } from '@tmt/browser-ui/blocks';

<BlockMenu label="Insert block" activeId={`insert-${active}`} placement={phone ? 'sheet' : 'below'}>
  <BlockMenuGroup>Basic</BlockMenuGroup>
  <BlockMenuItem id="insert-table" icon={<Table2 />} description="Columns and rows" shortcut="/table" active>Table</BlockMenuItem>
  {!matches.length && <BlockMenuEmpty>No block matches.</BlockMenuEmpty>}
  <BlockMenuFooter><span><BlockKbd>↑↓</BlockKbd> choose</span></BlockMenuFooter>
</BlockMenu>
<BlockMenu kind="actions" label="Block actions">
  {blockActions.map((action) => <BlockMenuItem key={action.id} shortcut={action.shortcut} danger={action.danger}>{action.label}</BlockMenuItem>)}
</BlockMenu>  // BlockMenuSeparator goes before Delete

390, light and dark

  • Hover and selection are tints; no outline except the keyboard focus ring.

pages.title: Insert a block
pages.html:
Insert a block

Type / on an empty line, or press the handle’s +: the insert menu lists the block types and filters as you type. ↑↓ choose, Enter inserts and puts the caret in the new block, Esc closes and keeps what was typed. On a phone it is a bottom sheet.

Handle and block menu

pages.html:
Keyboard selection

Esc leaves typing and selects the block; ↑↓ move the selection and Shift+↑↓ extend it; Delete, Cmd/Ctrl+D and Alt+Shift+↑↓ act on every selected block. There is no selection toolbar.
